text:
**Short version:** Qi2 is the open, magnetic wireless charging standard, Qi2.2 is its faster 25W update, and MagSafe is Apple's own branded version of that magnetic charging.

| | Qi2 | Qi2.2 (Qi2 25W) | MagSafe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who makes it | Wireless Power Consortium (WPC) | WPC | Apple |
| Max speed | 15W | 25W | 15W for most iPhones, up to 25W on newer ones |
| Magnets | Yes | Yes | Yes |

**Qi2** added a magnetic ring to Qi so the phone and charger line up, which improves efficiency and speed. Apple contributed its MagSafe tech to the standard ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)). It tops out at 15W ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**Qi2.2** is the same idea at 25W. The WPC says that's nearly 70% more power than Qi2, and it can charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). Technically it's Qi v2.2.1, and it's sold as "Qi2 25W." Look for that label on the box.

**MagSafe** is Apple's version. Per [Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html):
- Apple-certified chargers deliver 15W to most iPhones and up to 25W to iPhone 16 and 17 models.
- They also include an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify the charger, and a magnetometer to prevent compass interference.
- "MagSafe-compatible" chargers that aren't certified are usually just 7.5W with a ring of magnets.

Apple's latest MagSafe Charger is itself certified for Qi2 25W, so the two overlap at the top end ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8)).

**What you actually get depends on your phone:**
- **25W:** Apple lists up to 25W for iPhone 17, 17 Pro and 18 Pro models, plus some iPhone 16 models. The iPhone 16 and 16 Pro reach 22.5W, and the iPhone Air 20W. You need a 30W or greater power adapter ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)).
- **15W:** iPhone 12 through 15 and the iPhone 17e top out at 15W, even on a 25W charger.
- **Android:** Support is thin. The Pixel 10 supports Qi2 at 15W and the Pixel 10 Pro XL supports Qi2.2. Samsung's Galaxy S26 is "Qi2 Ready," meaning it needs a magnetic case to use Qi2 chargers ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

**Compatibility:** All of these are backward compatible. A Qi2.2 charger works on a Qi2 phone at the slower speed, and a Qi2 charger works on a Qi2.2 phone at 15W.

If you want a simple 25W option, the [Apple MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8) is $49 for the 2 m cable, and Macworld lists the 1 m at $39. The adapter is sold separately.
